NAM.note: No link between civil register and ID system is stated.
Governor speaks of an enabling fintech framework and an instant payment project, but states no mandate, licensing, switch oversight or PAPSS.
No civil registration system is described.
Only the central bank's own staff skills curriculum is mentioned, not a civil-service programme.
No consumer protection rule or complaints body is mentioned.
A CBDC for cross-border payments is only being explored; no corridor.

facts.fact: Bank of Namibia Governor Johannes !Gawaxab said the Civil Registration and Identification Bill was currently in Parliament.

NAM.note: Digital literacy is only mentioned as an emphasis; no public programme or survey.
Only the Bank of Namibia's own strategic plan (2022-2024) is mentioned, a ministry-plan type.
Automated government payment processing by the Bank is not payment to people.
No number at birth is mentioned.

facts.fact: The Governor said the Bank of Namibia developed a prototype e-KYC between private-sector and Ministry of Home Affairs databases for instant identity verification, to be fully implemented once the Civil Registration and Identification Bill is promulgated.
facts.system: e-KYC prototype (Bank of Namibia / Ministry of Home Affairs databases)
